extracted.intended_audience: aspiring improv/sketch students, performers, and readers interested in The Groundlings troupe and school
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and operational criteria for admission, advancement, membership, and performance expectations at The Groundlings improv and sketch comedy school and company in Los Angeles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission to Basic class (audition requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must pass an audition to get into the Basic class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a student passes the audition, their results are valid for one year. If a student does not pass the audition, they are allowed to audition again in four months. Students are allowed to audition a total of three times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program structure and levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The competitive program consists of five levels: Basic, Intermediate, Advanced Improv, Writing Lab, and Advanced Writing Lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants must satisfy instructors' requirements in order to advance from the first three levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement to Writing Lab and Advanced Writing Lab (Main Company voting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Admission into Writing Lab and Advanced Writing Lab is determined by votes of then-current members of the Main Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This vote is based on the students' writing and performing of Groundlings-style sketch shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat classes and time to complete program
rubrics_metrics.description: The program can take several years to complete; students may be asked to repeat Basic and Intermediate classes multiple times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No explicit maximum duration for the coursework is given, but advancement depends on satisfying instructors and peer voting for higher levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunday Company eligibility and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of Advanced Writing Lab, students may be voted into the Sunday Company where they write, rehearse and perform new material every week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sunday Company members are cast for six months at a time, can be voted into Sunday Company for a maximum of three six-month periods (no more than 18 months), and after six months may be voted to remain, dismissed, or voted into the Main Company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection into the Main Company
rubrics_metrics.description: All members of the Main Company are selected from members of the Sunday Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main Company members may remain as long as they desire (usually under a decade). The Main Company is capped at no more than 30 members and collectively acts as the organization's artistic director, democratically making business and creative decisions as a group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance output and show frequency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Different company tiers and shows have specific frequency and format expectations (e.g., Main Shows, Cookin With Gas, Crazy Uncle Joe Show).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main Shows (revues) are performed Fridays and Saturdays (8:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m.). Cookin With Gas is a weekly short-form improv show performed Thursdays at 8:00 p.m. The Sunday Company writes, rehearses and performs new material every week; historically the revue output increased from one or two per year to multiple per year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and technique expectations (Groundlings style)
rubrics_metrics.description: The troupe/school uses an improv format influenced by Viola Spolin and techniques taught by Del Close and members of Second City; these techniques are used to produce sketches and improvised scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students are expected to write and perform in 'Groundlings style' sketch shows (used as a basis for voting into higher labs and company membership).

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership selection and company size control
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership in the company is controlled by audition/selection to keep company size manageable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically the company required selection by audition as membership grew (example: membership grew to 90 and the company instituted auditions). The Main Company is deliberately capped (no more than 30 members) to maintain governance and creative direction.
